name: Printing Sequence of Numbers with a Gap Between Adjacent Values (Case 1)
description: Construct a program that prints a sequence of numbers from 1 (inclusive) to 16 (exclusive) in increments of 4.

comments.content:
We need to repeat printing the numbers that are in a sequence from 1 (inclusive) to 16 (exclusive). To do this, we need to use a loop structure. We use for loops instead of a while loop because we need to repeat the loop a certain number of times, and for loops are best-suited in cases like this when we know ahead of time the number of times that we need to repeat the loop. Here, we want the for loop to start counting from 1 with every fourth integer number up to but not including 16.

To do this, we initialize variable num to 1, loop until reaching 16 (exclusive), and increment num by 4 after each iteration of the loop.

In the first part of the loop header, we define a control variable num and initialize it to 1. In the second part of the loop header, we test whether the control variable has reached the termination threshold. The loop is repeated if the control variable is less than 16 and terminates when the control variable reaches 16. In the third part of the loop header, we increment the control variable by 4 after each iteration of the loop.

Note that the first part is executed once before the loop starts, the second part is executed before each iteration, and the third part is executed after each iteration of the loop.

Also note that the += operator adds the value on the the right-hand side of the assignment operator (i.e., 4) to the current value of the variable on the left-hand side (i.e., value of variable num) and that value is stored in the variable num. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement num = num + 4.
This statement prints each number in the sequence to the default standard output stream. Each printed value is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
